items.how: Make the status leave 'Checking...': show ready or not ready, or an error with a retry, within a bounded time. Re-enable 'Check if ready' once a check ends, and never leave it disabled with nothing to explain why.
items.why: o1.png and s1.png both show 'Status: Checking...' with the button greyed out and no message. The reader cannot learn if the book is ready, so check-ready is broken and the release proof line fails.

items.how: Give the reader view of a ready reservation a way to collect the book. Either add a collect action, or add a plain line saying to show this page at the front desk. Collection stays staff-only if the product wants that, but the reader needs to be told how.
items.why: s3.png shows the reader view with 'Ready at the front desk' and 'There is no link or button to collect the book', while the release goal says a reader can collect. o-collect.png shows 'Collect (staff only)' works, but only when signed in as desk staff, so the steps complete without the reader persona being able to use it.

sides.why: o-collect.png was walked signed in as desk staff, not as the reader persona the journey names.

sides.position: a reader finds no way to collect
sides.why: s3.png is the reader view and shows no link, button or instruction.

items.how: Make the Reserve button reachable at 1366x768 without scrolling: shorten the form or make the action bar sticky. Also confirm the focus order reaches the button early.
items.why: o2.png and s2.png show a five-field form filling the window, with a note that nothing below the bottom edge at 1366x768 is visible. The reserve step still completes by scrolling, and the smoke run did not test resize, so this is polish rather than a blocker.

items.how: The Captain decides whether 'Reserve a copy' or 'Hold a book' is the one label. Another walk should capture both labels in pictures before any change.
items.why: o3.png shows only 'Hold a book' on the reservation list and states the other label in text. No picture shows 'Reserve a copy' on the same action, and only one reviewer raised it.

items.how: The Captain decides whether to measure load time. Without a timing, do not change anything.
items.why: s4.png shows a fully loaded page and says it carries no timings, so the ten-second claim is a feeling no picture can settle.

deferred.how: Fold into i1: the status must refresh or time out with a message instead of staying on a stale 'Checking...'.
deferred.why: Both reviewers agree, and o1.png and s1.png show the stale status for two minutes, so the deferred risk is a real defect of the broken check-ready story.

No picture shows the button label, so its length cannot be judged. o's objection that it blocks them matches the below-the-fold problem, which is ruled in i3. Revisit the label only if the button's position is fixed and the label is still long.

deferred.how: Open the Button declaration at x.d.ts and look for a prop, slot or children that can supply what was declined. If one exists the decline is overruled. If only a custom build works, the Captain decides whether to accept a departure from the host's look.
deferred.why: The decline rests on a host component, and no picture shows the finding. I cannot check the declaration here, o agrees without a picture and s cannot tell, so I cannot uphold it.
